links.outcome: Reliability of LLM-assisted reference labels in MedCalc-Bench versus physician ground truth
links.effect: At least 27% of test labels likely erroneous or incomputable; on 50 physician-validated instances, original labels agreed with physicians 20% (95% CI 11-33%) vs 74% (60-84%) for recomputed labels; original labels underestimate LLM accuracy by 16-23 points.
links.quote: At least 27% of test labels are likely erroneous or incomputable.

unlisted_practices: Physician-in-the-loop stewardship pipeline to audit and recompute LLM-assisted benchmark labels
Training models on corrected labels (reinforcement learning) to improve downstream performance

screen.practice: physician-in-the-loop label auditing of LLM-assisted benchmark
screen.reason: Empirical audit and benchmarking of clinical LLM evaluation labels, demonstrating the impact of physician oversight/stewardship on benchmark label quality and downstream LLM evaluation.

primary.practice: physician-in-the-loop benchmark stewardship and label auditing
